text:
maya: FYI scheduling a short preflight for AZ4 01:00 UTC. Observed elevated nvme SMART warnings and packet retransmits from top-of-rack on racks 9-10 during nightly onboarding surge. Plan: small canary -> observe telemetry -> either continue with soft drains or abort. Expect ~8-15% GPU capacity reduction if we proceed.
sam: got it. which pools affected and how long window?
maya: pools: gradient-pool-b and batch-edge-az4. Window 01:00-01:45 UTC. Canary: rack-9 node-02 only.
infra-bot: [automated] maintenance scheduled: maintenance/6299991234-az4-nvme-preflight - 2026-03-22 01:00-01:45 UTC. Gate checks enabled.
leo: what are the gating thresholds? when do we stop?
maya: stop if nvme warn count increases >1 for the canary within 10m, or if WriteLatency p95 > 30ms for 5m, or if TCP retransmit % > 0.5% across the rack. Thermal OK threshold still 12C.
anika: question on cost: if we route cache fetch from other regions, what's the egress hit?
sam: estimate ~1.2TB cross-region = ~$110 for the short window if we backfill heavily. Try to keep local warm lanes.
david_ops: I'll prep a short customer status snippet at T-30m and tag any impacted partners.
harry_hw: NVMe vendor support ok to triage tomorrow AM, but if canary fails we'll need to swap the node. Spare blade availability low in AZ4—may need to RMA to adjacent colo.
leo: can we throttle new tenant onboarding during the window? Prefer avoiding cross-region egress.
maya: yes setting feature flag: /admin/features/pause_onboard -> true at 00:55 UTC until 01:20 UTC. Posting patch now.
infra-bot: preflight summary: kernel versions consistent; netcard microcode latest; nvme SMART: warning entries on rack-10 node-07 and rack-9 node-02. Node-02 flagged as canary.
maya: run sequence: 1) kick canary on rack-9 node-02 01:00 2) wait 12m telemetry window 3) if green, drain rack-9 nodes one-by-one with 4m spacing -> soft-reboot -> kv-cache seed. 4) verify route latency and API SLOs.
sam: suggest reducing kv_cache_seed_concurrency to 0.5 and temp max_batch_tokens=384 during warmup to avoid write storms.
maya: applying kv_cache_seed_concurrency=0.5 and max_batch_tokens=384 now.
leo: I'll add temporary dashboard annotation for per-route latency and token cost during the window.
anika: adding billing tag maintenance: az4-03-22 to any extra egress. Also flagging finance to expect ~+15% network bill for the day.
infra-bot: [update] canary started 2026-03-22T01:00:05Z on rack-9 node-02. Logs: /var/log/maint/6299991234-canary-node02.log
leo: early telemetry p95 write latency creeping to 28ms, nvme warn count incremented by 1. Holding.
maya: nvme warn jumped again, write latency p95 now 35ms and tcp retransmit at 0.7%. abort canary.
infra-bot: [automated] canary aborted 2026-03-22T01:08:23Z. All drains halted. Notifying hardware/contact harry_hw.
harry_hw: acknowledged. Opening HW ticket HW-51234 for physical inspection and spare allocation. ETA for swap: 2026-03-22 10:00 UTC (tentative) due to spare logistics.
david_ops: customer comm drafted: "We paused the planned maintenance after detecting increased NVMe warnings during our initial canary. No customer-facing errors observed. We'll update once hardware inspection completes."
anika: reverting provisioning pause? keep it active until we have HW confirmation that canary node is replaced.
maya: keep the pause. No cross-region failover. We'll reconvene at 09:00 UTC or on HW ticket update.
sam: I'm oncall 00:50-01:50 — standing by for infra-bot gate messages.
leo: creating follow-up remediation ticket infra-ops-629999 for scheduling long-term pool rotation and spare inventory review.
david_ops: thanks team. I'll post a customer update to status.redwood at T+30m.
maya: thanks all. Runbook: https://runbooks.redwood/az4-nvme-preflight. Will update channel with HW ticket link when available.
